subject: DPA: data routing, subprocessors & e-sign execution for Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps Team <legalops@bluepoint.com>, procurement@bluepoint.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is BluePoint's redline of Redwood's standard DPA plus our current subprocessor matrix. A few items we need clarified before we can proceed to signature:

1) Deployment modes: we require explicit DPA language covering Dedicated (Redwood-managed pools) vs Private/VPC vs on-prem. Our security policy expects that for Private/VPC the controller (BluePoint) can require specific data residency and will want the right to audit subprocessors if we host in our VPC. Can Redwood accept a tailored clause that distinguishes these modes?

2) Subprocessors: BluePoint requires 30 days notice and an approvals mechanism for any changes classified as "critical" (see attached matrix). We want to confirm your proposed subprocessors for Dedicated and Private deployments separately.

3) Cross-border transfers: BluePoint prefers SCCs + documented transfer mechanisms for EU data in Dedicated. For Private/VPC where data stays in our cloud account, we want confirmation there is no outbound transfer except for telemetry and billing (and that such telemetry is pseudonymized).

4) E-sign: can we finalize by DocuSign? We attached the redline PDF and the current subprocessor spreadsheet.

Please loop in whoever from your legal/ops side you need — happy to move quickly.

Best,
Sally Chen
Head of Legal Ops, BluePoint Financial

Attachments:
- BluePoint_DPA_redline_20261210.pdf (pdf)
- Subprocessor_Matrix_20261209.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Sally — thanks for the detailed redline and the matrix. We're committed to getting this done quickly. I'm looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Product/Infrastructure) to address the mode-specific items.

High-level responses now:
- Dedicated: Redwood-managed capacity will be treated as a subprocessors-managed environment; we can provide a subprocessors list for Dedicated and commit to 30 days notice for major changes.
- Private/VPC: if BluePoint uses our Private offering (customer VPC or dedicated tenancy), data residency can be constrained per your spec and audit rights can be scoped (we'll propose a tailored audit clause that balances your needs and our subcontractor constraints).
- Telemetry: we agree to minimize telemetry and provide a pseudonymization summary — will get Karthik to provide details.

Laura/Karthik — can you review the attached redline and the matrix and propose specific edits for the DPA (separate paragraphs for Dedicated vs Private) by EOD Friday? Also note Sally asked for DocuSign execution — that's fine from my side.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Business Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Vivek/Laura — quick technical notes to incorporate in the DPA edits:

1) Subprocessor separation: For Dedicated, subprocessors include (a) infra provider (GCP/AWS depending on region), (b) managed GPU provider (our fleet), (c) metrics/tracing vendor. For Private/VPC when BluePoint uses their cloud account and our control-plane, subprocessors are limited — most compute runs in customer tenancy; we only access logs/telemetry via authenticated connections. We can provide a per-deployment subprocessor manifest and a change-notice process.

2) Data flows: when customer chooses Private with on-prem option, there is no cross-border transfer unless customer authorizes. For Dedicated, data residency will be commensurate with region but infer requests may touch control-plane services in US (we'll add SCCs or equivalent).

3) KMS/HSM: For Private we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integrations; will add language to DPA referencing key management and that Redwood will not have plaintext access to keys.

I'll draft suggested language for the Dedicated vs Private paragraphs and attach a cleaned subprocessor matrix.

—Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Sally — thanks for the redline and the matrix. I've reviewed and propose the following changes (attached as a tracked-changes PDF):

- Section 2.1 (Definitions): add explicit definitions for "Dedicated", "Private/VPC", and "On-Premises" so obligations can be scoped per mode.
- Section 4 (Subprocessors): add subsection 4.3 describing a two-tier approval/notice process: 30 days notice for non-critical subs, immediate notice + impact assessment for critical ones. Critical subs will be enumerated in an annex.
- Section 7 (Cross-border transfers): we will accept SCCs for Dedicated where control-plane operations require it; for Private/VPC with customer-managed cloud accounts we will state that no intentional outbound transfers occur, save for pseudonymized telemetry and billing metrics.
- Section 9 (Audit & Access): propose an audit window and a redaction process for any Redwood logs that contain customer identifiers; audits scoped to Private deployments will be narrower and limited to the customer tenancy.
- Execution: Redwood is happy to sign via DocuSign; we'll prepare the final execution copy once redlines are reconciled.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_proposed_edits_20261211.pdf (tracked changes); Subprocessor_Manifest_Redwood_20261211.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps Team <legalops@bluepoint.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Laura/Vivek — appreciate the rapid turn. The proposed structure with mode-specific definitions + the two-tier subprocessor notice looks good. A few quick follow-ups from our side:

- Can you enumerate the "critical" subprocessors you propose to list in the annex? Our procurement will want to see names and locations (region).
- For telemetry, please add a short appendix describing what telemetry fields Redwood collects (IP, timestamps, usage metrics) and how you pseudonymize them. We need that for our internal privacy team.
- Please confirm the DocuSign link will be the standard BluePoint template (we will send the envelope once we have the final PDF).

If we can get the annex and telemetry appendix by EOD today we can route for signature tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sally
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BluePoint DPA redline and subprocessor questions (Dedicated vs Private)

Sally — attached are the requested annex and the telemetry appendix. Annex lists the "critical" subprocessors we anticipate using for Dedicated deployments (GPU fleet provider, infra provider, and metrics provider) with region hubs. Telemetry appendix enumerates fields and pseudonymization steps.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Subprocessor_Annex_20261214.pdf
- Telemetry_Appendix_20261214.pdf

If those look good I'll ask Laura to fold them into the final DPA.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@bluepoint.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:32:00 -0800
Subject: Final DPA ready for signature (DocuSign)

Sally — thanks for the swift review. We've incorporated the annex and telemetry appendix into the final DPA and uploaded a clean PDF to the shared Drive. Per BluePoint request, we've kept separate mode-scoped clauses and enumerated the critical subprocessors for Dedicated in Annex A.

We're prepared to execute via DocuSign. Please send your BluePoint DocuSign envelope and we'll sign on our side within the hour.

Final attachments: Redwood_DPA_final_20261214.pdf (pdf)
DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.net/Signing/?doc=ABC123456789

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
